record.context_brief: reanalysis of observational constraints for BSM messengers
record.original_question: If cosmological messengers of beyond-the-Standard-Model physics are confirmed through DAMA direct-detection data, LIGO-VIRGO-KAGRA gravitational-wave data, pulsar-timing-array stochastic gravitational-wave-background data, JWST early-galaxy observations, or AMS02 antihelium searches, how should existing observational constraints and the interpretation of the edges of those constraints be reanalyzed within BSM cosmology?

evidence.quote: The results of DAMA experiments, LIGO-VIRGO-KAGRA, PTA and JWST data, possible existence of antihelium component of cosmic rays increase the hints to new physics phenomena. Their confirmation will manifest deviations from the standard cosmological model.

The hints to the cosmological messengers of BSM physics may appeal to reanalysis of the observational constraints and interpretation of the edges of such constraints in the terms of the BSM cosmology.

artifact.status_search_result: The question is a broad research program rather than a single solved mathematical problem. No comprehensive reanalysis exists; the listed observational hints (DAMA, LVK, PTA, JWST, AMS-02) remain actively debated, and BSM cosmological interpretations are an open area of ongoing research as of 2026.

status_evidence.title: Open questions of BSM Cosmology (arXiv listing)
status_evidence.snippet: Review highlights that confirmation of these hints would require reanalysis of constraints within BSM cosmology.
status_evidence.claim: The reanalysis program is posed as an open direction rather than a solved problem.
